name: gemma_2b
_source: google/gemma-2b official config.json (HuggingFace) - verified against multiple independent mirrors, all identical: hidden_size=2048, num_hidden_layers=18, num_attention_heads=8, num_key_value_heads=1 (multi-query attention), head_dim=256, intermediate_size=16384, vocab_size=256000.
_gemini_vs_gemma: This is Gemma, NOT Gemini. Google has not published Gemini's exact architecture (hidden size, layer count, attention config, etc.) - it's a closed/proprietary model. Gemma is the openly-released model family built on the same research/technology as Gemini (Google's own description), and is the closest thing with a real, verifiable published config. If Google ever publishes exact Gemini hyperparameters, swap the numbers below - the block structure (transformer_layer with GQA/MQA) already generalizes to it.
_scope: Models one forward pass (e.g. prefill) over a seq_len-token prompt, covering every decoder layer's attention + gated-MLP projections plus the final LM head. Embedding lookup (a gather, not a GEMM) and RMSNorm/RoPE/softmax (no MACs) are not modeled, same convention as pooling/maxpool on the CNN side.
_notes: input.h=128 is the prompt length (seq_len) for this run - change it to model a different prefill length. It is NOT part of Gemma's published config; pick whatever you want to benchmark.
num_key_value_heads=1 means multi-query attention (MQA): all 8 query heads share a single key/value head - Gemma 2B's actual published design, not an approximation.

lm_head projects to the full 256,000-token vocabulary - this N far exceeds the 16-bit PARAM0 field limit (65535), so it only works correctly because model_to_npu_calls.py now tiles N as well as M (see --max-n-per-call).
